enonce_markdown:
Read the sentence below, then choose the word that correctly completes the fixed expression.

> During the heated meeting, Sarah remained calm and showed remarkable ___, even when her colleague raised his voice at her.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

Certains mots anglais se forment avec l'élément fixe self-, qui s'attache toujours de la même façon à un nom pour désigner une qualité ou une action tournée vers soi-même. Ces mots composés se mémorisent comme des blocs entiers, car leur sens ne se déduit pas du seul élément self-.

### Corrigé

The correct answer is **A) self-control**. This fixed compound means the ability to stay calm and control one's emotions, which exactly describes Sarah's behaviour during the heated meeting. Option B ('self-service') refers to a shop or restaurant where customers serve themselves; option C ('self-portrait') is a picture an artist makes of themselves; option D ('self-employed') describes someone who works for themselves rather than for an employer. All three are genuine self- compounds, but none fits the meaning of the sentence.

enonce_markdown:
Read the sentence below, then choose the adjective that correctly completes the fixed expression.

> My neighbour Grace has been my ___ friend since we were children; we still call each other every week.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

Certains couples adjectif+nom sont des collocations figées en anglais : un adjectif précis s'associe toujours au même nom pour exprimer une idée, même si un autre adjectif proche par le sens en français semble possible. Il faut mémoriser ces couples tels quels, sans les recomposer logiquement.

### Corrigé

The correct answer is **A) close**. 'A close friend' is the fixed collocation used to describe someone you are very attached to and trust deeply, exactly like Grace in the sentence. Option B ('near') describes physical distance, not friendship, and English speakers never say 'a near friend'. Option C ('short') and option D ('thin') describe size or physical shape, not emotional closeness, and neither collocates with 'friend' in English.

enonce_markdown:
Read the sentence below, then choose the phrasal verb that correctly completes it.

> Before you leave your bedroom in the morning, always ___ the lights and the television, so that no electricity is wasted during the day.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

Un verbe à particule (verbe + préposition) forme un bloc figé qui peut porter sur deux compléments reliés par 'and' à la fois, à condition que ce bloc garde un sens cohérent pour les deux éléments. Il faut repérer le verbe à particule qui convient réellement au contexte, et pas seulement à un des deux compléments.

### Corrigé

The correct answer is **A) turn off**. 'To turn off the lights and the television' means to switch both of them off, which matches the advice about saving electricity. Option B ('turn on') would mean the opposite, switching them on. Option C ('turn up') means to increase the volume or intensity of something, which does not apply to saving electricity. Option D ('turn over') means to flip something over, which makes no sense with lights or a television in this context.

enonce_markdown:
Read the English proverb below, then choose the sentence that best explains its meaning.

> "Don't judge a book by its cover."

What does this proverb mean?
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

Un proverbe anglais forme un bloc figé dont le sens global est souvent imagé : il ne se traduit pas mot à mot, mais se mémorise comme une unité porteuse d'un message précis. Il faut connaître ce message global pour reconnaître la bonne explication parmi plusieurs propositions.

### Corrigé

The correct answer is **A**. 'Don't judge a book by its cover' means that you should not form an opinion about someone or something based only on its outward appearance, because appearances can be misleading. Option B invents a literal meaning about reading instructions, which has nothing to do with the proverb. Option C and option D describe unrelated pieces of advice about organising books or lending belongings; neither reflects the real, figurative meaning of this well-known proverb.

choix.texte: You should not form an opinion about someone or something based only on how they look on the outside.
You should always read the instructions before using a new product.
It is important to keep your books and papers well organised.
You should never lend your personal belongings to strangers.

enonce_markdown:
Read the sentence below, then choose the compound word that correctly completes it.

> The school introduced a weekly sports session to improve the overall ___ of its students, both physically and mentally.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

Comme les mots composés en self-, les mots composés en well- forment des blocs figés à mémoriser individuellement : well- ne modifie pas le nom suivant de façon prévisible, et chaque combinaison porte un sens propre qu'il faut connaître par cœur.

### Corrigé

The correct answer is **A) well-being**. This compound means the state of being healthy, comfortable and happy, both physically and mentally, which matches exactly what the sports session is meant to improve. Option B ('well-known') means famous or widely recognised. Option C ('well-off') means financially comfortable, wealthy. Option D ('well-mannered') means polite and well-behaved. None of these three describes a state of physical and mental health.

enonce_markdown:
Read the short situation below, then choose the fixed expression that best completes it.

> Last year, Michael lost his job at the factory. At first he was devastated, but a few months later he found a much better position with higher pay and shorter hours. Looking back, he now says that losing his old job turned out to be ___.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

Plusieurs expressions idiomatiques anglaises partagent une construction similaire (article + nom + complément) mais ont des significations figées très différentes. Il faut connaître le sens exact de chaque expression comme un bloc entier pour choisir celle qui correspond réellement à la situation décrite.

### Corrigé

The correct answer is **A) a blessing in disguise**. This idiom describes something that seems bad or unfortunate at first but turns out to bring a positive result later, exactly like Michael losing his job and then finding a much better one. Option B ('a piece of cake') describes something very easy to do. Option C ('a shot in the dark') describes a guess or an attempt made without any real chance of knowing the outcome in advance. Option D ('a drop in the ocean') describes a quantity so small that it makes almost no difference to a much larger whole. None of these three idioms fits a situation that turns from apparently bad to genuinely good.
